text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/report.md
+**Health: unhealthy.** The frozen run completed 150 steps but obtained `val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1 = 0.0` on all 64 held-out examples at both steps 100 and 150. The final value is present in `observed_run/console-history.jsonl` (record 150) and `observed_run/stdout.log` (step 150 and final-validation output). It is not inferred from training reward or an earlier checkpoint.
+
+**Root cause — inconsistent per-token loss normalization at the verl/Megatron boundary.** The effective configuration enables `calculate_per_token_loss`, MoE router z-loss with coefficient 0.001, response-token-mean PPO and KL loss, dynamic microbatching, and CP2/EP2/TP1. These settings were retained. The implementation must distinguish the response-token count used by PPO from the full prompt-plus-response token count used by the router.
+
+The frozen metrics show optimization and generation collapse together:
+
+| Signal | Steps 1–50 mean | Steps 101–150 mean | Step 150 |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Training score | 0.29125 | 0 | 0 |
+| Response length | 229.71 | 985.67 | 1024 |
+| Response truncation ratio | 0.00375 | 0.91375 | 1.0 |
+| Gradient norm before clipping | 195.75 | 125.08 | 188.35 |
+| Generation time, seconds | 17.48 | 50.74 | 51.07 |
+
+At step 150, advantages and policy-gradient loss are zero; the reported actor loss is only 0.0002161, from KL loss 0.2161 times its 0.001 coefficient. Yet the gradient norm is 188.35 against a clipping threshold of 1. Router z-loss enters through Megatron's separate autograd path and is absent from that reported actor loss. Excess auxiliary gradients therefore can dominate clipping and continue moving the model after the reward-driven gradient disappears. This is a concrete reason to investigate normalization rather than increase the response limit or change the learning rate.
+
+The installed Megatron-Core 0.16.0 sources establish the mechanism: `transformer/moe/router.py::apply_z_loss` multiplies z-loss by the local token count in per-token mode; `pipeline_parallel/schedules.py::forward_step_calc_loss` expects a three-value `(loss_sum, num_tokens, metrics)` callback; `distributed/finalize_model_grads.py` sums counts across DP+CP and divides gradients only if that count is positive. A legacy two-value callback leaves the count at zero. A CPU regression using the actual scheduler and router confirms that such a callback amplifies the z-loss gradient by the global token count, even with a zero main loss.
+
+**Snapshot/evidence distinction:** the staged source already contained a partial three-value callback fix when this review began. I preserved it. The defects still present were:
+
+- The callback used `full_real_token_count // cp_size` on every CP rank. Packed sequences do not distribute their real tokens evenly when alignment padding is present. For sequence lengths `[5, 6, 8]`, the actual CP2 real-token counts are `[8, 11]`, but the staged callback reported `[9, 9]`. Its divisor was 18 for 19 real tokens; even the policy gradient was therefore scaled by 19/18.
+- The router received no padding mask, so its z-loss included alignment padding while the finalizer counted only real tokens. In the same example the router processed 24 rows, including five padding rows. This made the auxiliary objective depend on padding and microbatch partitioning.
+- A missing global token-count metadata field silently fell back to the microbatch count, which cannot preserve the global objective across unequal microbatches.
+
+These remaining defects are directly reproduced from the supplied code. They belong to the normalization failure implicated by the large gradients, disappearing advantages and truncation collapse. However, the frozen evidence does not record router-loss gradients or establish that the partial repair was used in the historical run. The rounding/padding errors alone do not prove the cause of the entire historical collapse. The fresh run is required to measure recovery; no training was launched during this review.
+
+Other inspected evidence does not support changing the prescribed experiment. Rollout/actor probability agreement improves: mean k3 KL falls from 0.002144 to 0.000294 across the two windows, while weight-transfer time stays near 65 seconds. Abort ratio is zero and all recorded numeric metrics are finite. Longer generation, rather than an increasingly slow weight transfer, accounts for much of the runtime degradation. GPU-capacity waits occur during startup; teardown errors occur after final validation. Data hashes match all five provenance entries; training has 7,473 rows, validation has the specified 64 indices, training/test questions are disjoint, prompts are intact, and gold answers pass the unchanged strict GSM8K scorer.
+
+**Changes — every changed or added workspace file:**
+
+- `src/framework/verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: added a router padding mask derived by packing real-token indicators with the model's existing THD/BSHD preprocessing. Passed that mask through model forward and its exact local real-token count to the loss callback, replacing integer division by CP size. Required the global mini-batch token count instead of silently substituting a microbatch count. Preserved the existing `loss * global_routed_tokens / dp_size` three-value callback and all configured losses. Kept the fused and value-head callers consistent with the shared callback.
+- `src/framework/verl/models/mcore/model_forward.py`: forwarded the supplied router padding mask to the model on the BSHD path, matching its existing THD support.
+- `src/framework/tests/workers/test_megatron_per_token_loss_on_cpu.py`: added CPU regression checks for exact CP counts, valid token ID zero, model-mask plumbing, ordinary/fused/value-head callbacks, unequal microbatches, DP1/DP2 and CP1/CP2 gradient equivalence, zero-main-loss auxiliary gradients, missing metadata, and legacy/forward-only contracts.
+- `report.md`: added this assessment, evidence, change inventory, validation and expected effects.
+
+**Expected effect.** Correct normalization should reduce excessive `actor/grad_norm` and clipping pressure while preserving the response-normalized policy objective and the configured z-loss. The intended held-out outcome is an increase in step-150 `val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1` above the frozen zero. Late `response_length/clip_ratio` should decrease from near 1, training reward should recover from zero, and generation time should fall as responses terminate normally. These are expectations, not measured post-repair results; the incremental benefit over the already-partially-repaired snapshot may be smaller than the historical failure suggests.
+
+**Checks and launch readiness.** The focused regression file plus the existing Megatron distillation tests passed: **29 tests**, CPU only, no model weights loaded and no optimizer steps. Test command: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src/framework:/workspace/scripts python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider src/framework/tests/workers/test_megatron_per_token_loss_on_cpu.py src/framework/tests/workers/test_megatron_distillation_only_on_cpu.py`. Python syntax checks and `bash -n scripts/train.sh` passed. Hydra composition with the launcher's actual overrides confirmed 150 steps, validation frequency 100, no step-0 validation, unchanged batches/seeds/model/data and CP2/EP2/TP1. The trainer explicitly validates the last step, so step 150 is included despite not being a multiple of 100.
+
+The frozen W&B file stops at step 148, as documented by `observed_run/logging-limitation.txt`; console evidence supplies the genuine final validation. The existing `scripts/runtime_lowmem.py` hook already flushes W&B after logging step 150. Its ordering was verified with an in-memory stub, without creating a W&B run. The unchanged launcher honors `TRAINING_RUN_DIR`, writes stdout to its `logs/train.log`, and writes offline W&B records under its `wandb` directory. No historical records were copied into run output. Frozen evidence, configuration, launch script, reward source and dataset hashes remain unchanged.
*** End Patch"));

steps.message:
The frozen run is unhealthy: held-out accuracy was 0 at steps 100 and 150.

Fixed CP token counting and router padding normalization; 29 CPU tests passed. Training was not launched, and frozen evidence and required experiment settings remain unchanged.

Report: [report.md](/workspace/report.md), including causal limits and expected metric changes.
